TARGET ENGAGEMENT: The trial shows evidence of target engagement - NIS expression increased from 21% to 25% (median), indicating that valproic acid did engage histone deacetylases and modulated gene expression. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The target was engaged and there was some downstream biological activity (NIS expression increase), but this was insufficient to achieve the intended therapeutic effect. The mechanism partially worked but didn't translate to meaningful clinical benefit. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite target engagement and some biological activity, the clinical endpoints failed completely - no patients achieved complete or partial response, and radioiodine uptake did not increase post-treatment despite NIS expression changes. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No meaningful subgroup responses were observed - only 1/8 patients had stable disease while 6/8 had progressive disease. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial appears adequately designed with appropriate duration (16 weeks) and dosing. No major confounders identified.
